correctness.rationale: For a nonempty digram set E, realizability is a directed covering walk on the looped simple digraph. Its SCC condensation is necessarily a path with precisely one inter-component arc on each transition, and this condition is sufficient. On at most three active vertices every strong component has balanced internal edges, except a 3-vertex strong component whose imbalances are in {-1,0,1} and sum to zero. Hence a directed Euler trail traverses all distinct arcs exactly once, yielding shortest length |E|+1. Classification by active vertices and SCC block sizes yields the explicit generating polynomial with coefficients 1,9,21,44,72,81,60,30,9,1 and total 328. The sole acyclic feasible digraphs are one empty, six single arcs, six oriented three-vertex paths; all other 315 supports admit an arbitrary-length extension from a cyclic terminal SCC or loop. Every n>=10 realizes all 315; no n<10 realizes the full 9-arc set. The four-letter word 02103101 gives six arcs with imbalance +2,-2 and exact minimum length 8. Standard-library independent word enumeration through length 10 and finite-state support-last-letter closure, executed from the included verify.py, reproduce all counts and witness claims. All-length statements are proved structurally, not extrapolated from enumeration.

evidence: Bernardini et al. give a general shortest walk algorithm and an O(k+n^2) output length bound, including cases that repeat arcs. Lemma 8 concerns strong graphs without sources/sinks and multiple distinct walks, not alphabet-three edge uniqueness.

These require the explicit small-component combinatorial analysis; there is no literal stronger theorem in the inspected primary text that implies the numerical claims without new evaluation.

originality.rationale: General set-valued k-substring shortest-string reconstruction via Eulerian covering walks and min-cost flow was already established by Bernardini et al. (preliminary CPM 2022), and is fully acknowledged. Their inspected accessible full text has no alphabet-three lossless-edge theorem, 328 support enumerator, fixed-length 315/13 persistence classification, or four-letter sharp obstruction. Recent genome k-mer representations are generally frequency-aware and provide motivation rather than this enumeration. The recovered nearest historical exact binary two-multispectrum result counts digram frequencies, which is not the binary digram presence set and does not imply the ternary classification. Actual targeted published-finding corpus queries and primary literature/search-engine searches found no equivalent or stronger claim. Limited coverage of unindexed results and an implicit special case of the general algorithm remain disclosed risks.
residual_risks: Unindexed or older exact enumeration of labeled three-vertex digraphs admitting a covering walk may already list 328 or equivalent counts.
The general graph-walk framework may make this special case accessible to existing software or an implicit consequence; the exact statements were not encountered in the inspected primary paper.
No independent third-party mathematical audit or complete bibliographic priority certification has been performed.

value.rationale: The alphabet-three versus alphabet-four threshold is a natural structural boundary of a standard reconstruction observable; all feasible ternary digram presence profiles admit lossless single-visit realizations, a property false for the next alphabet. The exact labeled classification and sharp fixed-length 315-class stabilization give motivated values for both minimal strings and finite-alphabet support-only reconstruction, and are not merely a reformulation of generic Eulerian-walk computability.
